brief: Tonight is Push B, and it is your fifth training day in a row — your last full day off was 29 July. That one fact shaped the whole card, so here is where it landed. Nothing goes up on either triceps lift. On Friday your triceps ran out inside the session: overhead extension went 53.75 for thirteen, then 55 for eleven, then 57.5 for only eight, and the rope pushdowns straight after went 60 for eight, 60 for seven, and then you dropped the weight. One of my trainers wanted all three overhead sets at 55 tonight. I took the other side. Same weights as your last Push B on both triceps lifts — 52.5 and 53.75 on the overhead, 23.75 and 27.5 on the reverse-grip — and one extra rep where the set fell short. Earn them with reps, not with the pin. Everything before the triceps does move, because you are fresh at the start of the night and you finished last Push B at the top of the range. Overhead press: 105, 115 and 120 for eight, then 125 for six. You pressed 105, 115 and 120 for eight last time and opened with 95 for ten, which is two reps past what that slot asks, so the whole ladder steps up one rung. Chest press is the big one: 165, 172.5, then 180 for eight. This is the largest jump on the card and I want you to know that before you sit down. You pressed 165 for ten on this day last week and 165 for twelve on Friday, so 165 is your opener now, not your top set — but 180 is the most the app will let me ask for, and if the third set stalls at six, that is information and not a failure. Lateral raises: the 12.5s for the first two sets, then the 15s. Last Push B you did the first two on the cable machine, so there is no dumbbell history for those sets at all and 12.5 is my best read, not a measurement — tell me if it is wrong. Crossovers stay at 25 and the ask is thirteen reps; all three sets stopped at twelve last time, which is the floor, so the weight has not been paid for yet. Reverse pec deck: all three sets at 90. Your first set hit fifteen at 82.5, the top of the range, so that set earned the plate. Dips: same three sets of twelve, but take one step less help from the machine — the app records dips as bodyweight and never sees the assist number, so I cannot print that setting for you. Now face pulls, because you asked me twice and deserve a straight answer. You were right and the program was wrong: face pulls were on four of your six training days, which is why you wrote what you wrote. That is already fixed — on 1 August you took them off Pull A and Pull B, and tonight is the first push day since. They now run twice a week, not four times. They are still on tonight's card at 30 for twelve, twice: you have done four sets in a row at 27.5 and stopped at exactly fifteen every time, which is the ceiling of the range doing its job, so the weight moves half a plate. If you want them off Push B for good there is a card below to say so, and your answer is final. Three more answers you are owed. You asked on 2 August whether three sets of hanging leg raises is correct. Three is what the plan asks, and both times you have done them your third set came in at ten after two twelves — ten is still inside the range, so it is not failing, but there is a card below to cut it to two if you would rather. You asked on 30 July why the calf raises wanted four sets. They do not. You had already been granted three back on 22 July, and the coach card that night overrode your own plan and asked for four anyway. That was our error, not yours, and the plan still says three. You asked on 30 July why the leg raises were written in seconds. Because when the plank was swapped out for them, they inherited the plank's stopwatch. That is fixed — Legs B now reads two sets of ten to twelve reps. Last thing, and it is the weakest part of your prep right now: I have one bodyweight reading in the last thirteen days, 206 on 21 July, and one cardio session in the last fourteen, fifteen easy minutes on the 21st. You are seven months out from the show. Step on the scale tomorrow morning and give me twenty to thirty easy minutes on any machine.

flags.note: Tonight is your fifth training day in a row — your last full day off was 29 July. Neither triceps lift goes up in weight because of it.
Face pulls: you were right. They were on four of your six days. That was fixed on 1 August when you took them off both pull days, and tonight is the first push day since — they now run twice a week.
Answering 30 July: the calf raises asked four sets because that night's coach card overrode your plan, which already said three. That was our error. The plan still says three.
Answering 30 July: the leg raises were written in seconds because they inherited the plank's stopwatch when they replaced it. Fixed — Legs B now reads two sets of ten to twelve reps.
One bodyweight reading in thirteen days (206 lb on 21 July) and one cardio session in fourteen. Week 3 of 4 in this build block, seven months from the show.

dissent.progression: 53.75 for thirteen reps on Friday is past the top of the range, so all three sets belong at 55 tonight
dissent.recovery: his triceps demonstrably ran out inside Friday's session at these exact loads, and tonight is his fifth straight training day — repeat the last Push B weights
dissent.why: Progression is right that 53.75 has been beaten. But recovery is the only seat holding evidence of what happened WITHIN a session, and it is specific rather than general: 53.75 for 13, 55 for 11, 57.5 for 8, then the rope pushdowns collapsed straight afterwards. Asking all three sets at 55 is more total load than the night that produced that fade, on a lift sitting seventh of nine in his longest session, on day five without a rest. I held the weights and asked for the reps instead.

dissent.progression: set one hit fifteen at 23.75, the ceiling of the range, so it earns 25
dissent.recovery: this is the second triceps movement of the night and the triceps are exactly what faded three days ago — same numbers as last Push B
dissent.why: Same ruling as the overhead extension and for the same reason; splitting them would be incoherent. This lift is eighth of nine, after six sets of pressing and the other triceps movement. Progression's claim is true — set one did hit the ceiling — but I am not spending a raise on the last triceps sets of a fifth consecutive training day. It keeps the weight and gets one more rep on the set that fell short.

dissent.progression: he finished 105, 115 and 120 all for eight — the top of the slot — and opened with 95 for ten, so the ladder steps up one rung
dissent.recovery: fifth straight training day and Push B is his longest session at 27 sets — repeat 27 July rather than climbing on top of it
dissent.why: Recovery's fifth-day argument is real and it decided the two triceps lifts. It does not decide this one. This is the first lift of the night on the freshest he will be, and the evidence for the raise is specific where recovery's is general: three of four sets at the ceiling of a six-to-eight slot, and an opener two reps past it. The top set only asks six reps. If day five is going to cost him something it will show here first, and he can stop at six.

dissent.progression: set one hit fifteen at 82.5, the top of the range, so that set earned 90 — all three at 90
dissent.recovery: with face pulls off tonight this is the only back-of-shoulder work in the session, so keep the weight where it was
dissent.why: Recovery's reason is conditional on face pulls coming off, and I did not take them off tonight — so the premise does not hold. On the merits only one set actually moves: he already did the second and third at 90, and set one hit the ceiling of the range at 82.5. That is the smallest raise on the card, on a light isolation lift, and it comes fifth in the session rather than at the tired end.

dissent.progression: four sets in a row at 27.5, all stopping at exactly fifteen because fifteen is the ceiling — the weight is too light
dissent.recovery: he has objected twice and the reverse pec deck already covers the back of the shoulder tonight — skip them
dissent.why: His complaint was frequency, in his own words, and it was answered on 1 August: he accepted taking face pulls off Pull A and Pull B, and they now run twice a week instead of four times. Tonight is the first push day since that change, so dropping them again would reverse a two-day-old decision he made himself, with no new fact since. What I will not do is decide it for him a second time — recovery's argument that the reverse pec deck already covers the same area in this session is a good one, so it goes to him as a card he can answer. Tonight they stay, at half a plate more, and the brief tells him plainly that he was right about the frequency.

proposals.why: Push B already has the reverse pec deck working the back of your shoulders, so face pulls are doing that job twice in one session — Push A has no reverse pec deck, so they stay on that day.

You asked whether three sets is right — both times you have done three on this day your third set came in at ten after two sets of twelve, so this makes it two if you would rather have the honest number.

You already approved moving this ahead of the Push A lateral raise on 23 July, but that card carried no position for the app to apply, so nothing moved and it still ran sixth on both Push A nights since — this is the same change with the number it was missing.

Dips are a pressing movement, but on Push B they run sixth, behind six straight sets of crossovers and rear-delt flies — this moves them up behind the chest press so both of your presses happen before the isolation work instead of after it.

overrides.reason: Every rung steps up one. You pressed 105, 115 and 120 all for eight last Push B, which is the top of what this slot asks, and your opener was 95 for ten — two reps past the ceiling for a set that heavy. The top set only asks six. This is the first lift of the night and the freshest you will be all session.

The 25.5 you typed is not a setting this machine has; 25 is the real pin plus micro. Beat thirteen on every set and the weight moves next time.
All three sets at 90. Your first set hit fifteen at 82.5, the top of the range, so that set earned the plate — the other two were already at 90. This is the smallest raise on the card.

It earns the raise with reps instead.
